newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS - Eurotunnel, banks agree on basic principles.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Eurotunnel, banks agree on basic principles.

text.p: Troubled Anglo-French Channel tunnel operator Eurotunnel Plc, which has not paid interest on its eight billion pound debt for more than a year, said on Wednesday it reached agreement in principle on a financial restructuring.

The company said that subject to approval from its board and banks, it expected particulars of the plan to be announced early next week. Its shares, which have been suspended, would then be allowed to resume trading.

"The co-chairmen of Eurotunnel, Sir Alastair Morton and Patrick Ponsolle, and the steering group of Eurotunnel's syndicate of banks consider that agreement has been reached on the basic principles of the restructuring plan which is essential for the group's financial recovery," it said.

Eurotunnel, which operates the rail tunnel between Britain and France opened in 1994, froze payments to 225 banks on its debt in September 1995, unable to cope with the loans and cost overruns incurred during construction of the link.
The debt market took relief. Eurotunnel bank debt offer levels were off slightly to 35 percent of face value from 37 percent after the news, which started filtering out on Tuesday night.
"This is positive in that no one really thought they'd come up with a plan by now and they have," a trader said.
The Paris commercial court confirmed the deal on basic principles, saying it had been informed that Eurotunnel and the lead negotiators for the banks had drawn up "the main lines of an agreement".
"The parties told the president of the Paris commercial court they hoped to submit a definitive protocol at a later date," said a brief statement from the court.
A source close to the debt restructuring talks said trading in Eurotunnel shares should resume by next Tuesday at the latest.

Once Eurotunnel's board and the banks have approved details of the debt refinancing and the information has appeared in the public domain, the shares should "requote Monday or Tuesday -- Tuesday by the latest," said the source.
Eurotunnel shares were suspended on Monday in Paris, London and Brussels to avoid creation of a false market while last-minute debt talks were being held with bankers.
Eurotunnel had been seeking a deal on the pricing of an expected debt-for-equity swap and the issue of convertible bonds, which would ease its debt service payments.
A debt deal would require shareholder approval.

In Paris, a Eurotunnel shareholders' group said it wanted to meet the company's management in the coming days once details of the debt agreement with banks were known so that it could decide its position on the deal.

"The association will carry out the necessary legal and financial analysis before deciding its position," the Eurotunnel Shareholders' Association, one of two groups fighting for a good deal for small shareholders, said in a statement on Wednesday.
"It will then call on its members and allies to vote in the direction that will be least unfavourable to their interest."
